_comment: Configuration for the Farm Water Analysis dashboard generator (lib/build_dashboard.py). Edit these values as the garden / irrigation plan changes; no code changes needed.

bed._comment: Physical geometry of the metered tomato raised bed, recorded 2026-08-03. This is the missing conversion that makes metered litres interpretable as inches of water. Everything metered by the WFC01 lands on THIS bed only; peppers are a separate unmetered line.

target._comment: target_in_per_week is Justin's stated goal. NOTE it is a classic in-ground, moderate-weather rule of thumb; a 10-inch-deep raised bed in a Santa Clara August loses considerably more. august_etc_in_per_week is the estimated real crop demand (reference ET0 ~0.25-0.35 in/day x tomato mid-season Kc ~1.15). Water to the ETc figure in a heat event and drift back toward target_in_per_week in Sept/Oct.

storage._comment: Plant-available water held by the whole 10-inch profile at an assumed AWC of 0.12-0.20 in per inch of soil. The point: a single 129 L dose is ~1.14 in, i.e. it tries to deliver most of the profile's ENTIRE available capacity in one 12-minute shot. That is why it drains.

emitters._comment: Audited 2026-08-03 against the measured 12.4 L/min line flow. Bubblers are adjustable 0-13 gph; back-solving from the meter puts them at ~13.4 gph each, i.e. WIDE OPEN, at or past spec. Do not throttle them far below ~half — the 8-stream full-circle pattern needs flow to distribute evenly, and a starved bubbler dribbles out one side. Use WFC01 cycle mode, not the bubbler threads, as the primary volume/rate control.

drip_flags.note: fixed rate; alone this is a 1.20 in/hr floor

infiltration._comment: The core problem found 2026-08-03. Instantaneous application rate is several times what the soil can absorb, so past the first minute or two water ponds, runs to the edges and channels down preferential paths instead of wetting the profile evenly. Effective (duty-cycled) rate should sit at or under the ceiling.

health._comment: Sensor-trust thresholds. nominal_volts is the voltage the probe's factory calibration assumes (1.5 V alkaline); a lithium AA reads ~1.7 V and shifts the derived moisture %. range_collapse_frac flags a probe whose daily AD swing drops below this fraction of its trailing norm (failing sensor or lost soil contact). volt_tolerance widened 0.08 -> 0.15 on 2026-08-09: a FRESH alkaline genuinely sits at 1.55-1.65 V, so 0.08 raised a false 'bad calibration' alarm on a healthy probe the day after the battery was restored. 0.15 still catches lithium (0.20 off nominal) while leaving normal alkaline headroom alone -- that gap is the whole discrimination this check exists to make.

plan._comment: Actual watering is a fixed timer, not a volume-based/Smart plan (that was never implemented). The WFC01 meters the tomato raised bed line ONLY. THE PEPPERS ARE NOT ON ECOWITT HARDWARE AT ALL — corrected 2026-08-19; they run off the HOUSE MULTI-ZONE IRRIGATION CONTROLLER alongside lawn/roses/trees. See pepper_system below before troubleshooting anything pepper-related. The pepper_freq/pepper_time/pepper_run_min keys live in this block for dashboard-rendering reasons only; they describe a different device on a different network with different failure modes. Delivery figures below are the MEASURED metered rate on clean days, not a nameplate estimate — real flow runs well above emitter nameplate.
plan.live_plan_note: ACTIVE as of the 2026-08-19 17:05 run, entered in the app by Justin on 2026-08-19; the first FULL day on the new plan is 2026-08-20, so use Aug 20 onward for any before/after comparison. Two plain-duration entries of 90 s each at 05:05 and 17:05, cycle mode OFF. The 05:20 and 05:35 morning pulses were REMOVED — 5-minute native traces showed the inter-pulse floor pinned at 79-81% (field capacity at the 3-inch probe) with pulse 1 alone reaching it, so pulses 2 and 3 spiked to 89-90% and shed it all back within 10 minutes without adding retained storage. Each 90 s run meters ~19.9 L, so ~39.8 L/day = 2.46 in/week, down from ~79.6 L/day = 4.92 in/week (a 50% cut). This lands at the top of the estimated August ETc band (1.75-2.45 in/wk) and is effectively ramp step 4. Metered figures here are ARITHMETIC (2 x 19.9), not yet measured — re-derive metered_daily/metered_weekly from clean days once Aug 20+ exports land. PM start moved 17:00 -> 17:05 as an incidental of re-entering the plan; immaterial.

schedule_log.change: PLAN LIVE — CUT TO TWO RUNS: 90 s @ 05:05 and 90 s @ 17:05, cycle mode OFF, entered in the app by Justin on 2026-08-19. ~39.8 L/day = 2.46 in/week, down from ~79.6 L/day = 4.92 in/week (a 50% cut). The 05:20 and 05:35 pulses are retired. This is the endpoint the ramp table called step 4 (37.2 L/day, 2.30 in/wk) and it sits at the top of the estimated August ETc band. FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION for Aug 20-22: 06:00 settled value 80 -> ~78; 17:00 daily floor 66-69 -> 63-65 (i.e. INTO the 60-68 ideal band, near the 62 setpoint); overnight plateau 73 -> ~70 and it should acquire a visible SLOPE instead of being dead flat. If the floor lands 62-66, STOP and hold. If it goes below 58, or midday wilt is still present at 20:00, restore one morning pulse. NOTE the pepper line was deliberately NOT changed on this date — see the pending pepper entry — so the tomato result is unconfounded.

MORNING PULSES 2 AND 3 ARE PURE WASTE — the Aug 5 'inter-pulse floor is flat' finding is now decisive at 5-minute native resolution, and the ambiguity it flagged has collapsed in the waste direction. Aug 18 trace: 05:00=72 (overnight floor), p1 05:05=75 -> 05:10=80, floor 05:15=79, p2 05:20=89 -> 05:30=81, p3 05:35=90 -> 05:45=81, then 06:00-06:55 flat at 79-80. Pulse 1 ALONE reaches the 79-81% field-capacity ceiling; pulses 2 and 3 spike 9-10 points above it and shed every point back inside 10 minutes. Same shape Aug 15/16/17/19. That is ~40 L/day and ~280 L/week buying zero retained moisture. The 'charging depth below the probe' alternative is now weakly supported at best: 89-90% at 3 in is near-saturation, which is ponding rather than downward movement, and the dead-flat overnight plateau (73.5 -> 73.0 across 6 h, ~0.08 pts/hr) says the profile is not draining downward either. STILL NOT PROVEN without the WH51L at 8-10 in — that remains the only instrument that settles it.

THE BED NEVER REACHES SETPOINT. Hourly means Aug 8-19: overnight 00:00-05:00 flat at 73.0-73.5, morning block peaks 77.8 at 06:00, daytime dry-down to a daily MINIMUM of 69.3 at 17:00, PM pulse resets to 74.6 at 18:00, then flat again. Setpoint is 62 and the ideal band is 60-68, so the daily floor sits 7-11 points ABOVE target around the clock and the bed spends zero hours in its own ideal band. Dry-down rate is 0.77 pts/hr in daylight vs ~0.08-0.15 pts/hr overnight. The dead-flat overnight line is itself the diagnostic: a profile that loses nothing across 11 h is not cycling, it is parked at capacity.

TIMING UNCHANGED, AND DELIBERATELY SO — 05:05 and ~17:00 both survive scrutiny; the lever here was volume, not clock. (a) Overnight loss ~0.1 pts/hr vs 0.8 pts/hr daylight means pre-dawn application costs essentially nothing evaporatively, re-confirming the Aug 2 decision. (b) The Aug 2 rationale (c) is now SUPERSEDED on its facts: that entry said the probe first registers the pulse ~06:00 and peaks 08:00, a ~2 h lag. At 90 s pulses the probe registers within 5 MINUTES and settles within 20, so there is no infiltration lag left to compensate for. The conclusion (do not move the start) is unaffected, but the reason is now simply the shared-pressure constraint plus the negligible evaporative penalty. (c) The PM slot correctly targets the daily minimum — evidence: the PM pulse peaks at only 76-80 vs the morning's 89-90, i.e. the bed is dry enough to actually absorb it. (d) SEPARATE TIMING ERROR FOUND: 15-minute pulse spacing is far too short. The bed returns to its floor within 10 min of each pulse and then sits there, so the 'soak' is over long before the next pulse lands. If two morning pulses are ever wanted again, space them 60-90 min, not 15.

PEPPER WASHOUT CONFIRMED — visible MID-RUN, and it validates Justin's unprompted instinct. The 15-min run is 06:40-06:55; Aug 19 5-minute trace: 06:35=40, 06:40=43, 06:45=58, 06:50=61 (peak), 06:55=53 — the probe is FALLING 8 points while water is still being applied — then 07:40=47 and parked at 46-47 all day. Same shape Aug 10/11/13/16/17/18. The media reaches container capacity ~5-8 minutes in; minutes 8-15 are leachate. Retained gain is only 40 -> 47 (+7 points) against a 21-point peak excursion. IMPORTANT COUNTERWEIGHT: nothing is stressed — peppers cycle 39 -> 47 entirely inside the 35-48 ideal band and never approach the 35 setpoint, so this is a water/nutrient efficiency fix, not a rescue, and there is no urgency. Also note SOME leaching is deliberate practice in containers (fabric bags accumulate fertiliser salts, Santa Clara water is moderately hard; standard leaching fraction is 10-20%), so the target is to reduce it, not eliminate it. Probe is at 2 in and therefore reads the TOP of the bag, which is the driest zone — bag bottoms stay wetter than 39%.

WRONG SYSTEM — Justin corrected a false assumption that had been sitting in this file unchallenged. The pepper bags are NOT on EcoWitt hardware; they are a zone on the HOUSE MULTI-ZONE CONTROLLER that also runs lawn, roses and trees. The same-day late-firing finding therefore ends with an ACTION THAT POINTS AT THE WRONG DEVICE ('count the schedule entries in the app' — there are no pepper entries in the EcoWitt app, and never were), and its 'two schedule entries' hypothesis was built for the wrong kind of controller. Superseded by the reframed entry below. See plan.pepper_system for the corrected device record. Every earlier note calling the pepper line 'a separate timer' was technically true and practically misleading — it read as a second EcoWitt-adjacent timer rather than a different system in a different troubleshooting domain.

PEPPER LATE-FIRING REFRAMED AS A HOUSE-SYSTEM FAULT — the observation stands, the diagnosis changes, and the stakes are higher than the peppers. THE OBSERVATION IS UNCHANGED: onset is bimodal at ~06:40 or ~07:20, 3 late days of 11 interpretable (~27%), full details in the preceding finding. WHAT THE CORRECTION KILLS: the 'tomato fired on time on the same hub' argument was overstated — the peppers were never on that hub, so it never ruled out a pepper-controller clock fault. What it DOES still establish is narrower but real: the anomaly is not site-wide (no power cut, no supply interruption), it is confined to the house controller. WHAT THE CORRECTION ADDS — THE KEY INFERENCE: on late days the pepper run is FULL SIZE, not truncated. Peak and shape match on-time days almost exactly (Aug 12 onset 07:20, peak 61 at 07:30, i.e. +10 min; Aug 19 onset 06:40, peak 61 at 06:50, +10 min). The zone gets its complete duration, just displaced ~40 minutes. A failing solenoid on the pepper zone would give a MISSED or SHORT run, not a perfect one 40 minutes late. Displacement of that kind, on a controller that runs zones SEQUENTIALLY, means something UPSTREAM in the sequence consumed ~40 extra minutes — an earlier zone running long, an extra program firing first, or a cycle-and-soak/seasonal-adjust setting inflating an upstream run. JUSTIN'S CONCERN IS THEREFORE WELL FOUNDED AND THE RIGHT WAY ROUND: the peppers are not the victim, they are the WITNESS. The missing 40 minutes went somewhere, and 'somewhere' is one of the unmonitored zones — lawn, roses or trees — being over-watered for 40 extra minutes on roughly one day in four, invisibly. DAY-OF-WEEK TESTED AND NOT SUPPORTED: late days are Wed/Fri/Sat, on-time days Sun/Mon/Tue/Thu/Wed, and BOTH Wed and Sat appear on both sides (Wed: Aug 12 late, Aug 19 on time; Sat: Aug 8 late, Aug 15 on-time-or-early). So this is not a clean alternate-day or 3-day-a-week program pattern. CAVEAT ON THAT NEGATIVE: 11 interpretable days gives only 1-2 samples per weekday, which is far too underpowered to rule a weekly pattern out properly — treat it as 'not supported', not 'refuted', and re-test once there are 3-4 weeks of clean data. No simple periodicity either (late-day gaps are 4 and 2 days). Intermittent with no schedule structure is consistent with Justin's failing-timer hypothesis.

HOUSE-SYSTEM TROUBLESHOOTING — NEXT STEPS, in order of information per unit of effort. (1) RECORD THE BASICS, currently all unknown: controller make/model, which zone number the peppers are, and the FULL ZONE ORDER with each zone's programmed run time. Zone order is the single most valuable missing fact, because the displacement hypothesis predicts the culprit is a zone that runs BEFORE the peppers. (2) SUM THE PROGRAMMED RUN TIMES of all zones scheduled ahead of the peppers and compare against the ~40 min gap — if one upstream zone is set to ~40 min, or an extra program adds ~40 min, that is the answer without any instrumentation. (3) CHECK FOR MULTIPLE PROGRAMS (A/B/C) with overlapping start times; overlapping programs on a single-valve-at-a-time controller queue rather than run concurrently, which produces exactly this intermittent displacement. (4) CHECK THE CONTROLLER'S BACKUP BATTERY AND FOR RECENT POWER INTERRUPTIONS — a controller that browns out and resets can re-run or shift a program. (5) IF THE CONTROLLER HAS A RUN LOG, pull it for Aug 8, 12 and 14 and compare against Aug 9, 10, 11 — that settles it directly. CHEAP INSTRUMENTATION OPTION: the WH51/WH51L hub has 8 soil channels and only 2 are in use. Putting a spare probe on the ROSES or a tree well would extend observability to a second house zone for the price of a sensor, and would show directly whether an upstream zone is over-running. That is the same argument as the WH51L depth probe in instrumentation_todo, applied to a different blind spot — and note the two compete for the same 6 free channels, so it is an ordering question, not an either/or.

PEPPER START TIME: NOT DRIFT, BIMODAL LATE-FIRING — and this entry CORRECTS the same-day claim that it was 'drifting ~40 min'. Drift implies progressive movement; onset is actually either ~06:40 or ~07:20 with NOTHING in between and no trend. Detected onset by first >=3-point 5-minute rise in a 04:00-10:00 window: 06:40-06:45 on Aug 9/10/11/13/16/17/18/19 (8 days); 07:20-07:25 on Aug 8/12/14 (3 days); Aug 7 at 09:15 excluded (battery-swap day, bags physically handled); Aug 15 UNINTERPRETABLE (export begins 06:40 mid-rise, only 40 of 72 expected samples in the window). So 3 late days out of 11 interpretable, ~27%. TWO FURTHER CORRECTIONS to the earlier claim: Aug 15 was a DATA GAP, not an early run — the 'fired before 06:40' reading was an artifact of the truncated export; and Aug 8 is a third late day that was missed entirely. TWO CAUSES RULED OUT: (1) NOT pressure starvation from another zone — on Aug 8/12/14 the probe is dead flat at 38-39 straight through 07:15 with zero rise at 06:40, then a FULL-SIZE jump; starvation would give a weak partial rise, not nothing. (2) NOT a hub clock fault — the tomato line fired on schedule on all three late days (Aug 8 05:00=78 -> 05:05=84; Aug 12 05:00=72 -> 05:05=84), same hub, correct time. The fault is specific to the pepper timer/valve. The offset is repeatably ~+40 min (07:20, 07:20, 07:25) rather than variable, which argues for something structured: BEST-FITTING HYPOTHESIS is TWO schedule entries on the pepper line, a primary ~06:40 and a second ~07:20 that only surfaces on days the primary fails to fire. ACTION: count the entries in the app.

PEPPER ONSET HISTORY IS UNRECOVERABLE BEFORE 2026-08-07 — worth recording so it is not re-investigated. The lithium battery flatlined the probe from ~Jul 22 to the Aug 6-7 alkaline swap (daily AD swing 4-7 counts vs 61-94 after), so it could not register a 15-minute irrigation event at all, and no onset time can be extracted from that window by any method. This means the ENTIRE life of the 'once daily 15 min @ 06:45' plan set on Jul 23 is invisible except for its last 13 days. Any question of the form 'when did this start / has it always done this' about the pepper line is answerable only from 2026-08-07 forward. General lesson, matching the Aug 4 dashboard fix: the cost of the dead sensor was not just wrong values at the time, it permanently erased the baseline needed to diagnose a later problem.

PEPPER CHANGE PENDING — NOT YET ENTERED. Justin is holding the pepper line at 15 min @ 06:45 for now and will cut to 7 min later. Target: ~7 minutes (about 5 min of delivery plus line-charge margin), keeping ONE 15-min flush every 2-3 weeks for salt management. FALSIFIABLE TEST, 4-5 days (NOT 2-3 — see the late-firing finding; at a ~27% anomaly rate a 3-day window is roughly a coin flip to catch one): if the settled value at onset+50 min holds at 46-47 AND the next-morning floor holds at 39-40, minutes 8-15 were pure drainage and the cut is free. MEASURE RELATIVE TO ONSET, NOT CLOCK TIME — a late-firing day shifts the whole curve ~40 min without changing its shape, so onset-anchored it is still a usable data point instead of a discarded one. If the floor starts declining day over day, split to 2 x 5 min rather than returning to 15 — fabric bags dry through the sidewalls and want frequency over volume. SIDE BENEFIT of the delay: the tomato two-run result stays unconfounded, consistent with proposed_plan.ramp.do_not_confound. BEFORE CUTTING: count the schedule entries on the pepper line in the app — see the late-firing finding for why there are probably two.

PULSED PLAN VALIDATED — the falsifiable prediction held. Predicted 2026-08-03: 'if the rate diagnosis is right, retained soil moisture should RISE while total volume FALLS.' Result over two days: water 124 -> 77 L/day (-38%), overnight minimum 50 -> 56 -> 57 (+7 points, reversing an eight-day slide from 58), daily mean 59.0 -> 67.8. The cleanest single comparison is the morning settled value at 06:00: Aug 3 delivered 129.4 L in one 12-minute flood and settled at 75%; Aug 4 and Aug 5 delivered 57 L in three 90 s pulses and settled at 78% and 79%. Less than half the water, 3-4 points MORE retained. The application-rate diagnosis is confirmed and the flood regime is retired.

MORNING PULSE STRUCTURE — pulses do stack at the peak but NOT at the floor. Aug 4: 63 -> p1 83 -> floor 79 -> p2 84 -> floor 80 -> p3 86 -> 78 at 06:00. Aug 5: 65 -> p1 84 -> floor 80 -> p2 86 -> floor 80 -> p3 88 -> 79 at 06:00. Each pulse peaks ~2 points higher than the last, but the inter-pulse floor is flat at ~80%, which is field capacity at the 3-inch probe. So pulses 2 and 3 add no storage AT THAT DEPTH. They are either charging the profile below the probe (the goal) or draining past it (waste), and a 3-inch probe cannot tell the two apart. The rising overnight minimum is weak evidence for the former, since water that left the system entirely could not still be present 24 h later — but the afternoon pulse is the more likely driver of that. THIS IS THE QUESTION THE WH51L AT 8-10 IN WOULD SETTLE, and it should go in alongside the pepper battery swap.

HOLD THE CURRENT PLAN — do not change the morning while the control variable is still improving. Overnight min is 57 against a 58-60 target and climbing; it is about to arrive on its own. Two days is also too little to re-tune on. Note total delivery is still 4.74 in/week against an estimated August ETc of 1.75-2.45, so there is likely substantial room to cut further, but the min governs, not the arithmetic. Afternoon pulse CONFIRMED NEEDED as Justin judged: it catches the bed at 56-57% at 17:00 and resets it to ~78% settled, which is what lifted the overnight floor off 50. Overnight bleed is now faster than historical (0.73 pts/hr vs 0.13) simply because the bed is wetter, which is expected and not a fault.

PEPPER PROBE CONFIRMED BAD — decisive evidence is behavioural, not electrical. Pepper water was HALVED on Jul 24 (every-12 h -> once daily) and the daily moisture swing did not change at all: it sat at exactly 1.0 point before and after, and has been 0-1 points every day since Jul 22. Over the same days the tomato channel swings 22-26 points. Halving the water of a real bed must deepen its dry-down; a probe that ignores a 50% cut in irrigation is not measuring soil. Daily AD range is 4-6 counts against 50-89 before Jul 22. The smooth ~0.7 pt/day decline from 44.7 (Jul 24) to 37.5 (Aug 3) is instrument drift with no diurnal structure. Swap to alkaline (1.5 V nominal) and confirm the AD range recovers before trusting any pepper number. Note this supersedes nothing about the calibration finding — the AD-to-percent mapping is shared and correct; the AD input itself is dead.

DASHBOARD FIX: the distribution panel was reporting 'Pepper — share of readings at or above the 35% setpoint: 100%, 0% below, min 35%' and the findings section called the peppers 'stable and dialed in'. Both were confidently wrong, and wrong in the dangerous direction: a flatlined sensor renders as a perfectly watered bed. The health module had already flagged the channel (ok=false, 2 warnings) but no other panel consulted it. Distribution cards and the pepper findings text now read DATA.health[k].ok and replace the statistic with an explicit 'sensor flagged' state. General lesson for this dashboard: any panel that states a confident summary must first check instrument trust.

PLAN LIVE: four plain-duration entries of 90 s each at 05:05, 05:20, 05:35 and 17:00, cycle mode OFF, entered in the app on Aug 3. ~19.9 L per pulse => ~79.6 L/day = 4.92 in/week, down from ~129 L/day = 8.00 in/week (a 38% cut). The three morning starts 15 min apart are a manual cycle-and-soak using Plan mode's 24 start times — a 15-minute soak, far longer than WFC01 cycle mode could give, and it sidesteps the unresolved On>Duration validation bug entirely. Deliberately conservative because Justin is off-site until Aug 6.

CLOSED: the dashboard irrigation panel has been rewritten. It now renders the multi-start schedule from plan.runs, states delivery in inches per week against bed geometry, shows the metered week converted to inches, and the dashed benchmark line tracks the new plan rather than the retired 14-min timer. The stale '14-min run / ~820 L / no volume target' narrative is gone.

BED GEOMETRY RECORDED (12 x 4 ft, 48 sq ft, soil 10 in deep) and it overturns the prior read of this system. 1 inch of water over the bed = 113.3 L. Current delivery of ~124-129 L/day is therefore ~1.1 in/DAY = ~7.7-8.0 in/WEEK, against a stated target of 1.0-1.5 in/week — roughly 6x over. A single dose is ~1.14 in, close to the entire plant-available capacity of the 10-inch profile (1.2-2.0 in), delivered in 12 minutes. The bed has never been under-watered; it has been flood-dosed daily, which is why the probe spikes to 90%+ and sheds 15 points in 45 minutes.

ROOT CAUSE: application RATE, not duration or timing. Measured line flow 12.4 L/min over 48 sq ft = 6.6 in/hr instantaneous, vs 0.2-0.6 in/hr for loam and maybe 1-3 in/hr for a loose raised-bed mix. Past the first minute or two water ponds, runs to the edges and channels rather than wetting the profile. Emitter audit: 9 drip flags @4 gph = 136 L/h fixed (a 1.20 in/hr floor on their own), leaving the 12 adjustable bubblers at ~13.4 gph each — wide open, at or past their 13 gph spec.

SUPERSEDES the Aug 2 'next lever' entry (7 min AM + 7 min PM). That was written without bed area and would have delivered ~174 L/day = 10.7 in/week — worse than the problem it was meant to fix. Ignore it.

NEW PLAN (WFC01 cycle mode as the primary rate control, NOT the bubbler threads — an 8-stream full-circle bubbler throttled too far loses its pattern and dribbles out one side). Cycle 30 s ON / 90 s OFF = 25% duty = 1.65 in/hr effective, which sits inside the raised-bed infiltration window. Run ~6 min elapsed (~1.5 min of actual flow, ~18.6 L) twice daily at 05:05 and ~17:30 => ~37 L/day = 0.33 in/day = 2.30 in/week. That targets estimated August ETc (1.75-2.45 in/wk), not the 1.0-1.5 in/wk shoulder-season figure. Step down over ~5 days rather than cutting from 129 L in one go, and watch the overnight min. FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION: if the rate diagnosis is right, retained soil moisture should RISE while total volume FALLS, because a larger share of a smaller dose actually infiltrates. If the overnight min keeps dropping as volume comes down, the diagnosis is wrong and the deficit is real.

DECISION: keep the tomato start at 05:05 PT rather than moving it toward sunrise (06:13 on Aug 2, drifting to 06:25 by Aug 16). Original motive for the early slot — avoiding overlap with the property's other zone timers — holds up. Rationale: (a) the water-at-sunrise rule is a foliar-disease argument and does not apply to soil-level bubblers/drip-flag emitters; (b) measured overnight loss is ~0.13 pts/hr (60.4 @18:00 → 59.0 @05:00) vs ~1.1 pts/hr daytime (71.7 @08:00 → 60.4 @18:00), so pre-dawn application costs ~nothing evaporatively; (c) infiltration lag already lands the recharge where you'd want it — the 3-in probe first registers the pulse ~06:00 and peaks 08:00, about 2 h AFTER sunrise, so a later start would only push peak deeper into the demand curve; (d) control here is timer-based, and daily draw already varies 106–128 L (CV 5.5%, implied flow 10.6–12.8 L/min), so moving into the shared-pressure window would add flow variance to the one variable being calibrated by minutes. Also avoids confounding the 10→12 min change taking effect Aug 3.

NEXT LEVER if 12 min fails to lift the overnight min back into 58–60%: split the dose rather than adjusting time-of-day or adding more minutes to a single run. The 07:00–11:00 plateau at 70–71% reads as the bed sitting at field capacity and shedding the excess, which is a percolation loss that a longer single run would worsen. Try ~7 min @ 05:05 + ~7 min mid-afternoon at similar total volume; this also stays clear of the other zones' morning window.

10-min run confirmed at 118 L/day measured over the 9 clean 10-min days Jul 24–Aug 1, vs 168.6 L/day at 14 min — ratio 0.70 against the theoretical 0.714. metered_daily/metered_weekly are now MEASURED 10-min figures (118 / 825, the latter an actual observed Jul 26–Aug 1 seven-day total, not an extrapolation) and the old 14-min estimate note is retired. The back-filled Jul 26 export resolved what looked like a 229.8 L spike on Jul 27 into two normal days (123.6 / 106.2).

Tomato timer raised 10 → 12 min once daily @ 05:05 PT, effective the Aug 3 run. Rationale: at 10 min the tomato daily mean fell steadily 64.6 → 60.5 over Jul 26–Aug 1 (−0.68 pts/day, ≈ −4.8 %/wk vs the −0.6 %/wk 34-day regression) and the overnight min broke below the 58–60% watch band to 53 — the trim over-corrected for current ET. Expect metered draw to rise to roughly 142 L/day / ~990 L/wk (118 × 12/10); re-measure and update metered_daily/metered_weekly from clean days once the next exports land. Watch that the overnight min recovers back into 58–60%.

Pepper probe battery swap (lithium 1.70 V → alkaline 1.50 V) scheduled for later the week of Aug 3. Pepper moisture is NOT trustworthy until then: AD range has collapsed to 4–6 counts (was 50–89 before Jul 22) with daily min/max nearly identical, i.e. no diurnal signal at all, so the apparent Jul 27–Aug 1 decline (43.8 → 40.5) reads as calibration drift rather than a real dry-down. After the swap, confirm the AD range recovers before acting on any pepper number.

DECISION: hold peppers at once daily 15 min through the week of Jul 27 despite an apparent net daily deficit (AD baseline −3 to −4 counts/day vs only +2 recovery per dose). Pepper probe is on a lithium battery (1.70 V vs 1.50 V nominal) since Jul 18, so its % scale is shifted and its AD range has collapsed — deficit reading is unconfirmed. Escalation tripwires handed to on-site helper; re-evaluate on the Aug 1 site visit.
Pepper bags moved from every-12 h to once daily, 15 min @ 06:45 PT; watch the 2-in probe for a deeper daily dry-down (bag bottoms may still stay wet).
Tomato timer trimmed 14 → 10 min to cut leaching / deep percolation; watch the overnight probe min holds near 58–60% at 3 in.
Tomato timer set: 14 min once daily @ 05:05 PT (fixed-timer, replacing earlier irregular hand-timing).

proposed_plan._comment: NOT YET ACTIVE — proposed 2026-08-03 after reading docs/Ecowitt Water Meter WFC01.pdf. Set this in the Ecowitt app, then move these values into the live keys above. Manual refs: sec 6.1 watering methods p22-23, sec 6.2.2 cycle mode p24-25, sec 6.2.3 plan mode p27-30.
proposed_plan.method: BY DURATION (Justin's call, 2026-08-03). Volume mode was tried at install and rejected: emitter output is uneven across the flags and bubblers, and he reads timings more fluently than volumes. Accepted — distribution unevenness is real but it is orthogonal to the control method (a given emitter's SHARE of the total is the same whether the run ends on a clock or on a quantity), and operator fluency has genuine value. One thing duration keeps that volume would have destroyed: under volume mode the metered-litres chart flatlines by construction and loses its value as a leak/clog detector. Under duration, metered volume drifting at a fixed run length IS the diagnostic. The cost is that delivered depth is no longer guaranteed — recheck metered L against the target weekly and re-trim minutes.

cycle_mode.REVISED_2026-08-03: Was 20/60. Lengthened to 45/135 (same 25% duty, same 1.65 in/hr effective rate) after Justin raised line-charge time. The hose must fill and the bubblers must reach pressure before real delivery starts; a 50-100 ft run holds 1.9-8.6 L depending on ID, which is 9-42 SECONDS of charge at 12.4 L/min. Against a 20 s pulse that is most of the pulse. Rule of thumb: ON >= 4-5x measured charge time. 45/135 cuts charge events per run by ~2.3x while keeping the effective application rate identical, because infiltration cares about the cycle-average rate, not pulse length. Per-pulse application at 45 s is 9.3 L = 0.082 in, which a 135 s soak clears comfortably at 1.65 in/hr.
cycle_mode.charge_accounting: RESOLVED 2026-08-03 with actual plumbing: 25 ft of 5/8 in garden hose = 1.51 L = 7.3 s of fill; the emitter manifold inside the bed adds ~0.96 L; total cold-start fill ~2.5 L / ~12 s. Crucially the hose runs UPHILL into the raised bed, so the emitters sit at the high point. When the valve closes, air enters at the bubblers and the hose water CANNOT flow back up over the crest — the 1.51 L in the hose simply stays there between pulses and between runs. It is never lost and never re-paid. Only the ~0.96 L above the crest drains, and it drains INTO the bed, so it is delivered rather than wasted. Net: NO volume is lost anywhere in this system. Within a run the effective re-charge is only the above-crest volume, ~5 s, so a 45 s pulse carries ~11% deadband on pulse one and near zero after.
cycle_mode.uniformity_finding: The real cost of cycling here is not volume, it is WHERE the drain-down lands. The ~0.96 L above the crest empties out of whichever bubbler sits lowest, once per cycle. At the originally proposed 20/60 that is 22 drain events/day and ~21 L/day preferentially dumped on one or two plants; at 45/135 it is 10 events and ~9.6 L/day; at 90/270 it would be 4 events and ~3.8 L/day. This is very likely a large part of why emitter output looks so uneven. 45/135 is the chosen middle: longer pulses cut the skew, but they also deepen transient ponding per pulse (0.082 in at 45 s vs 0.164 in at 90 s), which pushes water laterally to the bed edges. MITIGATION: find the lowest bubbler and either raise it level with the others or fit a small check valve just past the crest.
cycle_mode._comment: Manual: 'a duty cycle is introduced against the current working mode... can be used to regulate more precisely for lower water rate application.' Legal range 5-3600 s. 25% duty takes the 6.6 in/hr instantaneous rate down to ~1.65 in/hr effective, inside the raised-bed infiltration window. 20/60 gives ~4.1 L per pulse; 15/45 is a finer alternative at the same duty.
cycle_mode.RESOLVED_semantics: The app rejects On > Duration ('the on time cannot be greater than the duration'). That validation only makes sense if Duration is the total ELAPSED window that the pulses run inside — so Duration = elapsed, NOT ON time. The 4x ambiguity is settled and the duration_s column in the ramp table stands as written.
cycle_mode.APP_UNIT_TRAP: Entering Duration 360 s with On 45 s / Off 135 s was rejected even though 45 < 360. Near-certain cause: the Duration field has a unit selector (manual p25: '10~43200 seconds OR 1~720 minutes') that was sitting on MINUTES, so the form held 6 while On held 45, and the validator compared the raw numbers 45 > 6. FIX: switch the Duration unit to seconds and enter 360. If Plan mode only offers minutes, the only way to satisfy a naive numeric compare is On <= the minute number, which forces ~5 s pulses — volumetrically equivalent (On 5 / Off 15 for 6 min still gives 18.6 L) but useless here, because a 5 s pulse is roughly the above-crest refill time so nearly every pulse would be pure line charge.

ramp._comment: Justin's concern about shocking the plants is well taken, though the mechanism is not 'shock' from the volume cut per se — plants respond to root-zone moisture, not to applied litres, and the 10-to-12-min test showed +5.2 L moving settled moisture by -1 point, so most of the marginal water never reaches roots. The real risk is that the 2.35 in/wk ETc estimate is simply too low for a raised bed in a heatwave, while the probe is already at a record-low 50%. Abrupt swings also invite blossom-end rot and fruit cracking, so gradual is right regardless. THE PROBE SETS THE ENDPOINT, NOT THIS TABLE: hold at whatever step returns the overnight min to 58-60%, even if that is 70 L/day and the 38 L target turns out to be wrong.
ramp.TEST_RESULT_2026-08-03: 90 s plain run at 17:00 (no cycle mode) delivered 19.9 L (13.3 L/min at the meter) and took the probe 53% -> 87%. The same morning, 129.4 L took it 50% -> 90%. So 6.5x the water bought 6 more points of peak. If ~20 L rewets the profile then ~110 L/day is surplus — about 766 L/week. This is the strongest single piece of evidence in the whole record that the bed is being flood-dosed, and it was obtained without a stopwatch.
ramp.AWAY_PLAN_2026-08-04_to_06: Justin is off-site until Thu 2026-08-06, so: no stopwatch, no physical inspection, no charge-time measurement, and cycle mode is still unverified in the app (the On>Duration rejection is unresolved). Do NOT deploy unverified cycle mode unattended in a heatwave. Instead use PLAN MODE's 24 start times as a manual cycle-and-soak with plain duration runs, which is proven working hardware as of the 17:00 test. Entries: 05:05, 05:20, 05:35 and 17:00, each 90 s. That is 4 x 19.9 = 79.6 L/day = 4.92 in/wk, down from 8.00. A 15-MINUTE soak between pulses is far better than the 135 s that cycle mode would have given, and it directly serves the 'deep but not past the 10 inches' goal: repeated small increments infiltrate and redistribute downward between doses, whereas one 12-minute flood exceeds infiltration, ponds, and channels. Deliberately a conservative 38% cut rather than the full ramp — err wet while nobody can look at the plants. Re-evaluate Thursday on site.
ramp.OPEN_QUESTION_depth: Unresolved and NOT answerable from a 3-inch probe: 19.9 L is only 0.176 in of water, which cannot uniformly wet a 10-inch profile from depleted, yet the probe at 3 in jumped to 87%. That means fast preferential/macropore flow, not a uniform wetting front. So a small dose reaching the probe does NOT prove the bottom of the profile is charged. This is exactly what the WH51L depth probe at 8-10 in would settle, and it is the main reason to keep the away-period cut conservative.
ramp._units: ALL THREE APP FIELDS IN SECONDS: On time 45 s, Off time 135 s, Duration in seconds. One cycle = 180 s and delivers 9.3 L at the measured 12.4 L/min. Duration is always a whole number of cycles (n x 180) so no run ends mid-pulse. To change VOLUME adjust the cycle count (Duration); to change RATE adjust Off time; leave On time alone once it is set from measured charge time.

table_at_25pct_duty.note: single PM run on 2026-08-03 only — resolves BOTH the Duration semantics and the line-charge time

ramp.low_end_note: Steps 4 and 5 collapse at this cycle size — 2 cycles is the practical floor for a 2x daily schedule. If the probe asks for less than ~37 L/day, drop to ONE run per day at 2-3 cycles rather than shortening pulses, since shorter pulses would put charge overhead back in.
ramp.measure_charge_time: On the test run: start a stopwatch at valve open, note (a) seconds until the FARTHEST bubbler is running full and (b) the meter delta at that moment — that is charge time and charge volume. Then at valve close, note how long emitters keep dribbling. If charge time exceeds ~11 s, raise On time to 4-5x it and raise Off time to keep the 25% duty.
ramp.if_duration_means_on_time: If the 2026-08-03 test shows Duration counts ON time rather than elapsed, DIVIDE every duration_s above by 4 (i.e. duration_s = cycles x 20). Setting 880 s under an ON-time reading would deliver ~182 L per run = ~364 L/day, roughly 3x the current over-application — which is why the test run comes first.
tripwires: Overnight min falls more than 2 points the day after a step -> hold, or back up one step.
Overnight min recovers into 58-60% -> STOP RAMPING and hold there, whatever the litres say.
Midday wilt still present at 20:00 -> back up a step immediately (midday wilt that recovers by evening is normal).
Blossom-end rot or fruit cracking appearing -> moisture is swinging too hard; lengthen hold_days_per_step.
Metered L/day drifting at a fixed run length -> emitter clog or leak, not a schedule effect.
ramp.do_not_confound: Leave the pepper line untouched through the ramp, and do not also change start times or duty cycle mid-ramp.

caveats: Plan-mode skip conditions (rain skip, temperature skip) are NOT implemented — manual p28 says 'under development'. Do not design around them.

Smart mode (auto-irrigate from the WH51 reading) requires the hub to be talking to the Ecowitt cloud. Hold off until a depth probe is installed; closing the loop on a 3-inch probe would just automate the current misread.
Scheduled plans ARE stored locally on the hub and survive network outages (manual p17).
The WFC01 manual is written for the GW2000 hub; this garden runs a GW1200. It works, but expect minor UI differences.

instrumentation_todo.add_depth_probe: The WH51L ships with a 1 m / 3.28 ft PVC cable specifically to 'enable the measurement of different depths of soil moisture' (manual sec 3.2). Installing one at 8-10 in in the tomato bed permanently settles whether extra run minutes are wasted or are charging the deep root zone — the current 3-inch probe cannot distinguish those. WH51 and WH51L share the same 8 soil channels; only 2 of 8 are in use.
instrumentation_todo.soil_calibration: Both probes are on FACTORY calibration. Back-solving the tomato AD/percent pairs gives 0%AD=124, 100%AD=352 (0.438 % per AD count). Pepper AD 211 predicts 38.3% against an observed 38%, so the two probes share one calibration and there is no voltage-induced shift in the AD->percent MAPPING. SCOPE CORRECTION (2026-08-09): that result was over-generalised on Aug 3 into 'the lithium-battery theory is wrong'. It only ever tested the mapping, never whether the battery shifts the raw AD counts the probe emits — which is upstream of the conversion, and is where the effect actually is. See pepper_probe_battery_finding. Factory 0%AD is the AD in air and 100%AD is submerged in water, so both ends are wrong for real soil; manual states 'generally, the sensor must be calibrated to suit your soil type' (Custom mode, WH51L sec 3.3).
instrumentation_todo.pepper_probe_battery_finding: RESOLVED 2026-08-09: the pepper flatline was the LITHIUM AA, not a failed probe. Daily AD swing by battery phase — alkaline to Jul 17 (v 1.50->1.28): swing 48 down to 16; lithium from Jul 18 (v 1.70): AD floor steps 225->199 with no soil event, swing good 4 days (50/66/89/57) then collapses Jul 22 to 4-6 counts and the floor drifts monotonically 241->203 for two weeks; alkaline restored Aug 6-7 (v 1.60): swing recovers 61/89/88 within a day. A clean 2-week monotonic ramp with no diurnal cycle is not soil physics. CAVEAT: the 4-day lag between the Jul 18 swap and the Jul 22 collapse is unexplained — the AD floor makes a second discrete step (199->241) on Jul 22 — so the battery is clearly implicated at the recovery end but may have interacted with a reseating or contact event at onset. Keep the probe on alkaline; health.nominal_volts 1.5 +/- 0.08 correctly flags 1.70 as out of tolerance.
instrumentation_todo.pepper_probe_heat_hypothesis: RULED OUT 2026-08-09 on SIGNATURE, not on temperature magnitude. The theory was that a black fabric bag in full sun exceeds the WH51/WH51L 122 F spec ceiling. Decisive test is the hour-of-day profile of pepper AD, which needs no temperature data at all: a heat-ceiling dropout must be DIURNAL — normal at dawn, degrading through the afternoon, recovering overnight as the bag cools. Observed mean AD by hour, peak-to-trough: alkaline Jul 1-10 = 13.3 counts; lithium Jul 23-Aug 5 = 3.9 counts (flat ~222 across all 24 hours, no dawn rise, no afternoon decline); alkaline Aug 7-9 = 30.4 counts, peaking hour 10 and declining normally through 12-16. The probe is fully responsive DURING peak-heat hours on the restored battery, and was equally dead at 4 a.m. as at 4 p.m. under lithium. That is a supply fault, not a thermal one. Soil contact and depth are still worth checking on their own merits.
instrumentation_todo.wfc01_temp_is_not_ambient: CAUTION added 2026-08-09 after an analysis error. The [WFC01] Water Flow Temperature column in the EcoWitt exports is the METER'S OWN BODY TEMPERATURE sitting in direct sun — it ran 110-123 F through late July while Santa Clara ambient was nowhere near that. It is valid for the wfc01_heat note below (that note is about the unit overheating itself) and useless as an air-temperature proxy for anything else. Ambient weather for the dashboard comes from the keyless Open-Meteo API fetched client-side, not from the log files; use that for any real weather question.
instrumentation_todo.wfc01_heat: The WFC01's own temperature sensor read 123.1 F on 2026-08-03, its highest on record. The unit's Overheating alert fires at 60 C / 140 F (manual sec 7.4). It is sitting in direct sun and heading toward its own alarm threshold — shade it.

pepper_system._comment: RECORDED 2026-08-19 after Justin corrected a wrong assumption in this file. The pepper fabric bags are NOT on EcoWitt hardware — they are a zone on the HOUSE MULTI-ZONE IRRIGATION CONTROLLER that also runs lawn, roses and trees. Every prior note that spoke of the pepper 'timer' as if it were an EcoWitt plan entry was wrong about the device, and the 2026-08-19 'count the schedule entries in the app' action pointed at the wrong system entirely. This is a separate troubleshooting domain: different controller, different valves, different failure modes, no API, no logging.
pepper_system.controller: house multi-zone irrigation controller (make/model NOT YET RECORDED — write it down on the next site visit, along with the zone number the peppers sit on and the full zone order)
pepper_system.pepper_zone_number: UNKNOWN — needed. Zone ORDER is the key unknown, because a multi-zone controller runs zones sequentially and any upstream zone running long displaces everything after it.
pepper_system.metering: NONE. The WFC01 does not see this system. There is no flow data, no run log, and no remote status for any zone on it.
pepper_system.telemetry_note: IMPORTANT CONSEQUENCE: the WH51 pepper soil probe is the ONLY instrumentation of any kind on the entire house irrigation system. It was installed to watch pepper moisture, but because it registers each irrigation event it is in effect an accidental run-log for one zone — and the only observability into a controller that also waters the lawn, roses and trees. Treat pepper-probe anomalies as candidate house-system events, not just plant-moisture events. Corollary: the Jul 22 - Aug 6 lithium-battery flatline blinded not only the pepper channel but the only sensor on the whole system.
pepper_system.shared_pressure_note: The 05:05 EcoWitt tomato start was originally chosen to avoid overlapping this system's morning window (see the 2026-08-02 decision). That rationale is now MORE important, not less: the two systems share supply, so house-side zone changes can affect measured WFC01 flow on the tomato line.
